summary.headline: Fast premium growth, but profit depends on the Maldives and the Sri Lanka business loses money; fair value about Rs 6
summary.text: Amana Takaful (ATL.N0000) is a Shari'ah-compliant (takaful) insurance group: general takaful in Sri Lanka, 55% of Amana Takaful (Maldives) PLC, 76.3% of Amana Takaful Life PLC and a start-up in Uzbekistan. Premiums are growing fast (group gross written contribution up 38% to Rs 13.41bn in nine months of 2026), but owners' profit fell 58% to Rs 227mn (EPS Rs 0.89 against Rs 2.21), with a Rs 189mn loss in the third quarter. Most of the profit comes from the Maldives subsidiary; the Sri Lanka general business lost money on its own in 2024, 2025 and 2026. Owners' ROE was 7.9% in 2025 (13.0% in 2024) against a 16.5% cost of equity, and no dividend has been paid. At Rs 22.30 (30 September) it trades at 1.02x NAV of Rs 21.89. On normal owners' profit of about Rs 0.40bn (EPS Rs 1.35, ROE about 6–9%), three methods put fair value at Rs 6.02. Buy up to Rs 5.12; Rs 4.52 or less is a strong buy. Category 3, avoid for now: it fails the returns, steady-profit and cash/dividend tests.

models.name: Justified price to book
models.comment: (Long-run ROE − growth) ÷ (cost of equity − growth) × NAV Rs 21.89: 0.14x / 0.35x / 0.78x book, with ROE 6% / 9% / 13% and growth 4% / 5% / 6%. A long-run ROE below the 16.5% cost of equity is worth less than book.

models.name: P/E method (justified)
models.comment: 2027 EPS Rs 0.70 / 1.35 / 2.15 (owners' profit about Rs 0.21bn / 0.40bn / 0.64bn) × the justified P/E at the cost of equity, payout 1 − g ÷ ROE: 2.4x / 3.9x / 6.0x. All three are well above the Rs 0.14 twelve-month run-rate, which includes the cyclone-hit fourth quarter of 2025 and the third-quarter 2026 loss.

models.name: Residual income
models.comment: Used instead of a cash-flow DCF, which doesn't suit an insurer. Book Rs 21.89 plus profit above the cost of equity: ROE moves in a straight line from 6.2% to 6% / 9% / 13% over ten years with nothing paid out (no dividend), then the excess return grows at 4% / 5% / 6%. Keeping all profit at an ROE below the cost of equity lowers value, so this is the lowest method.

modelsNote: An insurer's cash flows are mostly premiums and claim reserves, so instead of a cash-flow DCF I used residual income and a justified price to book, alongside P/E, all at the 16.5% cost of equity (18.0% / 15.0% bear / bull) and all worked by scripts/valuation.py. No dividend model: the company pays no dividend. Growth check: long-run growth of 4% / 5% / 6% against 8.3% supported (94.9% of 2025 profit kept × 8.8% ROE); all within 2 points, and paid for by profit kept. Long-run growth stays below the 12.24% bond yield. Every method lands well below book because normal ROE (9% base) is far below the cost of equity.

scenarios.common: Cost of equity from the house formula (risk-free 8.24% + beta 0.80 × 10.28% equity premium). Bear: the Maldives stays at its weak 2026 pace and Sri Lanka keeps losing money; base: the Maldives recovers part-way and Sri Lanka is near break-even; bull: Sri Lanka turns profitable and ROE returns to 2024's 13%. 299.5m shares after the May 2026 rights issue. Stated under SLFRS 4; SLFRS 17 may change book value and the timing of profit.

sensitivity.title: Justified price to book, base case, Rs per share
sensitivity.note: Book × (ROE − 5%) ÷ (cost of equity − 5%). Today's Rs 22.30 needs a lasting ROE of about 16.5%, the cost of equity, which the group hasn't reached in the years read.

buyPlan.note: About Rs 2,422 in total, against Rs 11,150 for 500 shares at Rs 22.30.
buyPlan.realism: Not realistic: Rs 5.12 is 77% below the 30 September price. The 2026 low to September was Rs 19.10, the 2025 low Rs 11.70, and the rights issue was priced at Rs 19.00. Worth an alert only; the case changes if the Sri Lanka business becomes profitable and ROE rises well above 13%.

higher: The Sri Lanka general business making a profit on its own for a full year.
Owners' ROE back to 13% or more (the 2024 level) with the larger, post-rights-issue equity.
A disclosed capital adequacy ratio comfortably above the 120% minimum.
An SLFRS 17 contractual service margin showing the in-force book is worth more than book value.
lower: Further quarterly losses like the third quarter of 2026.
A weaker Maldives subsidiary, which carries most of the group's profit, or a weaker rufiyaa against the rupee.
Another rights issue to support capital.
Heavy start-up costs or capital needs in Uzbekistan.

fullText:
**Amana Takaful PLC (ATL.N0000): first analysis, 26 November 2026**

**Summary.** A fast-growing takaful (Islamic insurance) group whose profit comes mostly from its 55%-owned Maldives subsidiary, while the Sri Lanka general business loses money on its own. Owners' profit fell 58% to Rs 227mn in nine months of 2026 (EPS Rs 0.89), with a Rs 189mn loss in the third quarter, and no dividend has been paid. On normal owners' profit of about Rs 0.40bn a year (EPS Rs 1.35, ROE about 6–9%) and the house cost of equity of 16.5%, fair value is **Rs 6.02**. Buy up to **Rs 5.12**, strong buy at **Rs 4.52** or less. At Rs 22.30 (30 September 2026, the latest price available to this run) the share is almost four times fair value. Category 3, avoid for now: only one of the four business tests passes.

**The business.** Four parts (Annual Report 2025, PDF pp. 94, 139):
- Amana Takaful PLC itself: general takaful in Sri Lanka (motor, medical, fire, marine), gross written contribution Rs 5.76bn in 2025.
- Amana Takaful (Maldives) PLC, 55% owned: general takaful, GWP Rs 5.43bn, profit Rs 933mn in 2025 (parent's share Rs 513mn). The parent's share of its net assets is Rs 3.80bn, about Rs 12.7 a share.
- Amana Takaful Life PLC, 76.3% owned (listed separately): family takaful, mostly unit-linked, GWP Rs 1.76bn; about break-even.
- Amana Sugurta, Uzbekistan, 79%: a start-up (revenue Rs 46mn in nine months of 2026).

The company's own accounts carry the subsidiaries at equity value. Its profit less its share of subsidiaries shows the Sri Lanka general business alone: −Rs 61mn (2024), −Rs 117mn (2025, with Cyclone Ditwah claims) and −Rs 165mn (nine months of 2026).

**Latest results (nine months to September 2026, unaudited).**
- Gross written contribution Rs 13.41bn, up 38% (company Rs 5.69bn, +27%; medical +46%, fire +146%). Retakaful ceded up 69%, so net earned contribution rose only 17% to Rs 8.65bn.
- Claims and benefits Rs 5.50bn (+29%); administration costs Rs 2.50bn (+23%); investment income Rs 833mn (−11%).
- Profit before tax Rs 616mn (Rs 1,085mn); owners' profit Rs 227mn (Rs 546mn). Third quarter: owners' loss Rs 189mn.
- Maldives pre-tax profit Rs 740mn (Rs 1,038mn), and only about Rs 9mn of it in the third quarter.
- Rights issue of Rs 1.0bn in May 2026 (52.85m shares at Rs 19.00); 299.5m shares now. Owners' equity Rs 6.56bn, NAV Rs 21.89.

**Valuation (Rs per share).**

| Method | Bear | Base | Bull | Weighted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Justified price to book | 3.13 | 7.61 | 17.03 | 8.15 |
| P/E (justified) | 1.67 | 5.22 | 12.86 | 5.68 |
| Residual income | 1.08 | 3.48 | 10.84 | 4.23 |
| **Fair value** | | | | **6.02** |

Weights 30 / 50 / 20. Cost of equity 18.0% / 16.5% / 15.0% (beta 0.80, provisional). No cash-flow DCF (an insurer) and no dividend model (no dividend). All three methods worked by scripts/valuation.py.

**Assumptions.**

| | Bear | Base | Bull |
|---|---|---|---|
| Owners' profit 2027 | Rs 0.21bn | Rs 0.40bn | Rs 0.64bn |
| 2027 EPS | Rs 0.70 | Rs 1.35 | Rs 2.15 |
| Long-run ROE | 6% | 9% | 13% |
| Long-run growth | 4% | 5% | 6% |

Base assumes the Maldives recovers part-way from its weak 2026 and the Sri Lanka business gets near break-even. Bull returns ROE to 2024's 13%. Growth check: 4–6% long-run growth against 8.3% supported by profit kept (94.9% × 8.8% ROE in 2025). The twelve-month EPS of Rs 0.14 is far below all three cases because it holds the cyclone quarter and the third-quarter loss.

**Why so far below the price.** The group earned 13.0% on owners' equity in 2024 and 7.9% in 2025, against a 16.5% required return. An insurer that earns less than its cost of equity is worth less than book, and the rights issue added Rs 1.0bn of equity before profit grew. The 55% Maldives stake alone is about Rs 12.7 a share of book and earned about 15% in 2025, but the rest of the group loses money. The price assumes the group can earn its cost of equity, which it hasn't done in the years read.

**Business tests (1 of 4: weak, category 3).**
- Returns: fail (7.9% in 2025, about 1% in the latest twelve months).
- Capital and borrowing: pass on borrowing only (subordinated debt Rs 0.16bn, net cash). The company's capital adequacy ratio isn't disclosed, and the rights issue was raised to improve it.
- Steady profit: fail (owners' loss in 2023, losses in Q4 2025 and Q3 2026).
- Cash and dividends: fail (no dividend in 2024, 2025 or 2026 so far).

**Buy plan (500 shares).** 200 at Rs 5.12 or less, 150 at Rs 4.80, 150 at Rs 4.52: about Rs 2,422 in total. Not realistic this year: the 2026 low to September was Rs 19.10 and the 2025 low Rs 11.70. Set an alert only.

**Management and shareholders.** Management is promising growth through more branches, bancassurance and digital channels, and premiums are rising fast. But it gives no profit or return targets, and nine-month profit fell 58%. The Kassim family (several accounts) and Amana Bank PLC control the company. In the third quarter, Senthilverl Holdings sold about 27m shares and a new holder, Mr Mohomad Aslam Omar, took 27.0m (9.01%).

**What would change the view.** Higher: the Sri Lanka business making a profit on its own, ROE back to 13% or more, a first dividend, a disclosed capital ratio well above the minimum. Lower: more quarterly losses, a weaker Maldives subsidiary, another capital raise, or SLFRS 17 cutting equity.

**Uncertain.** The price is the 30 September market price from the interim report, because the CSE close couldn't be fetched from this run. The beta is provisional, and the March 2026 interim wasn't among the downloaded reports.
